title: Tokenizer impact — mini experiment & ad-hoc heuristics
content:
Notes to self / quick experiment log — goal: surface high-impact tokenizer-induced label mismatches and try tiny heuristics we can later bake into preprocessor or QA rules.

Context:
- We keep seeing label disagreements that correlate with tokenization boundaries (subword breaks, URLs, punctuation). This is a quick runbook + findings doc to capture examples, small counterexamples, and candidate fixes.
- Intended audience: me (Ethan), Maya, annotators doing the next labeling batch. Not a final guideline, just fast experiments.

Summary of experiments run (local):
- Dataset sample: 5k sentences pulled from prod-ish corpus (customer support + docs).
- Tokenizer: byte-level BPE variant from model-x (same as serving model).
- Tooling: small python scripts using tokenizers library + our label-compare script.
- Metric used: fraction of label spans where token boundaries cause split inside the labeled span ("token-split-rate") and fraction of annotator disagreement where a token boundary aligned with the disagreement ("boundary-linked-disagreement").

Results (quick):
- token-split-rate: 3.6% overall (higher in code/URLs: ~12%).
- boundary-linked-disagreement: ~28% of disagreements had at least one token boundary inside one annotator's span but not the other's (suggests tokenization matters).
- Top offenders: camelCase identifiers, long hyphenated compounds, emoji sequences, inline code snippets, product SKUs (alpha-numeric tokens), and URLs with query strings.

Representative examples and proposed micro-decisions (examples drawn from sample):
1) "SetAuthTokenX-23 to true"
   - Raw: SetAuthTokenX-23
   - Tokenized to: [Set, Auth, Token, X, -, 23] (split hyphen and alnum)
   - Annotator A labeled whole compound as ENTITY (product token), B labeled only "SetAuthTokenX" (dropped -23) => disagreement tied to hyphen/num split
   - Decision: treat hyphenated alpha-num compounds as single token for labeling heuristics when pattern = [letters][mixed alpha-num][dash][digits] and length < 40.
   - Heuristic: pre-join via regex before tokenization for labeling preview (but keep original text for final output).

2) URL with anchor/params: "https://example.com/guide?id=23#section-2"
   - Tokenized: protocol, domain, slash, guide, ?, id, =, 23, #, section, -, 2
   - Annotators disagree on whether to include the fragment "#section-2" in the ANCHOR span.
   - Decision: normalize URL anchoring rule: label entire URL as single span only if intent is URL-type entity. If label is just a route/name, allow separate smaller spans. Add a note in UI: "include query/fragment?" prompt on ambiguous URL-like labels.

3) Emoji sequences: "Thanks 🙏🏽 — fixed"
   - Tokenized: emoji split into multiple codepoints; sometimes skin-tone attaches or splits differently across tokenizers.
   - Observed: annotator A included the whole emoji sequence in SENTIMENT span; B only marked the text token.
   - Decision: canonicalize emoji sequences using unicode grapheme cluster normalization before labeling. Treat grapheme clusters as single tokens for span-consistency checks.

4) Inline code and backticks: "Use `my_func()` to start"
   - Tokenized: backticks separated in many tokenizers; parentheses and underscore cause split.
   - Annotators disagree on whether punctuation is included in CODE span.
   - Decision: annotate code spans to include surrounding backticks and immediately adjacent parentheses if whole contiguous code-like string. Add QA rule: if left/right neighbor is backtick (or triple backticks), include them.

Quick regex cheats (to try in preprocessor):
- join-hyphenated-alpha-num: (?<=\b)([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]{2,20}-[0-9]{1,6})(?=\b) => replace with placeholder token __JOINED_HYP_S1__{original}__
- url-squash: (https?://[^\s]+) => mark as single URL token for labeling preview
- emoji-cluster: use python's regex with \\X (grapheme) to coalesce sequences

Small script commands I used (notes to reproduce):
- python experiments/token-boundary_analysis.py --input samples/5k-sample.jsonl --tokenizer modelx-bpe --out debug/boundary_stats.csv
- grep counts: head -n 50 debug/boundary_stats.csv | sort -k3 -n

Annotation UI changes to reduce these disagreements (low-effort):
- show tokenized preview toggle next to span selection (annotator can see how the serving tokenizer would split the span).
- when selected text contains patterns matching join-hyphenated-alpha-num or url-squash, show inline tooltip: "Tokenizer will split this into X tokens — consider expanding/contracting span".
- small checkbox: "Include surrounding punctuation" when selecting spans (defaults: off for plain text, on for code/URL heuristics).

QA checks we can add to pipeline (post-label submission):
- Flag if span contains non-grapheme boundary splits (emoji grapheme detection) -> manual review.
- Flag if span contains >1 tokenization boundary inside and span length < 8 chars -> probably labeling error.
- For labels that match our product SKU regex, require double-confirmation (2 annotators) OR majority rule if tokenization indicates probable split.

Open questions / risks: 
- Pre-joining before tokenization helps labeling consistency but might hide real model behavior (serving model will still see split tokens). So if we pre-join for labeling only, we must ensure downstream model sees consistent reconstruction.
- How much do we want to encode in the labeling UI vs training-time augmentations? Both have costs: UI is slower but provides human intent capture; training-time heuristics can be faster but opaque.
- Edge cases where pre-join makes multi-entity span that should be separate (two adjacent product codes). Need heuristics to detect that (e.g., if both halves are in product dictionary, do not join).

Quick plan for next week (minimal actionable):
- 1) Run expanded sample (30k) to get per-label-type token-split-rate. (Owner: me)
- 2) Prototype tokenized preview toggle in annotator UI (Maya) — small UX: show native tokenizer spaces, not change selection logic.
- 3) Add three QA flags to pipeline (Liam) and run on a held-out labeled batch.
- 4) Draft short micro-guideline doc for annotators (1 page) with 6 rules: hyphen+num, URL include rule, emoji normalization, code punctuation, SKU double-confirm, and example gallery. (Owner: me/Maya)

Small gallery of borderline examples for the micro-guideline (copy-pasteable):
- "OrderRef-777" => product sku: include entire string.
- "OrderRef-777/backup" => ambiguous: if slash present, split at slash unless both sides match SKU regex.
- "api.getUser()" => include parentheses if contiguous with identifier.
- "Check `-v` flag" => include backticks and dash.
- "pm@example.com" => email: label full email as single span.

Notes-to-self: 
- write unit test that simulates annotator selection + tokenizer preview => compute agreement increase if we auto-suggest expansion.
- coordinate with serving-team: confirm tokenizer version pinned in model config (so preview matches inference).
- communicate with docs: add small FAQ about when to include punctuation in entity spans.

References (quick links):
- Slack thread: #data-ops TsK9f3 (where Maya flagged the first batch)
- GH PR: label-tools/pull/88 contains the small preview script used here
- JIRA: DATACLEAN-412 is the epic to track preprocessor heuristics

TODO (short):
- [ ] Run 30k expanded analysis by 2026-03-14 (Ethan)
- [ ] Maya: prototype tokenized preview by 2026-03-21
- [ ] Liam: add QA flags and run on batch by 2026-03-18
- [ ] Draft 1-page micro-guideline and circulate to annotators by 2026-03-20

Last quick thought: prefer conservative heuristics that err on the side of NOT merging across strong semantic separators (slash, comma in lists). We want higher precision in label spans even if recall needs augmentation via model-side canonicalization.

-- E.C.
